Neha / Alyssa — quick summary from Finance + Compliance. High level: yes, we can comply with deletion requests for user-identifiable request logs while preserving the financial artifacts necessary for accounting and audits. Details and operational steps below.

1) Invoices and ledger entries (billing amounts, invoice numbers, tax lines)
   - Retention: Redwood retains invoice PDFs and corresponding ledger entries for a minimum of 7 years to meet tax and accounting obligations in our primary operating jurisdictions. These records are immutable for the retention period and can be exported as PDFs/CSV on request.

2) Usage telemetry and request-level logs
   - Default customer-facing telemetry (request text, prompt/response payloads, client IPs, user identifiers) are considered data subject to deletion requests. We will delete raw identifiable records on confirmation of the DSAR (data subject access request) unless a legal hold applies.
   - For billing reconciliation, we keep a separate "billing ledger" which stores aggregated usage amounts and transaction identifiers (invoice_id, usage_bucket_id). That ledger does not retain raw prompt text or IPs.

3) Reconciliation identifiers and pseudonymization
   - To balance deletion and accounting, we can: 
     a) keep hashed/pseudonymized user IDs (salted hash) that allow BrightLeaf to reconcile invoices with their internal IDs without restoring PII, or
     b) provide a one-time export of reconciled rows (invoice_id, timestamp, aggregated token count) and then purge the reconciled temporary file after delivery.

4) Audit & legal hold
   - If BrightLeaf is under an audit or regulatory investigation, we recommend placing a short legal hold (we can implement an internal flag) that freezes deletion for a defined scope. Please note legal holds require an authorized request from your legal or finance team.

5) Timeline & operational ask
   - If BrightLeaf confirms they want the DSAR processed while keeping invoices: we propose the following operational flow:
   • Redwood exports invoice artifacts + a reconciliation CSV (invoice_id, billing_period, total_tokens, amount, hashed_customer_id).
   • We deliver that export over the secure transfer method you prefer (SFTP / signed DocuSign link / Redwood Console).
   • Upon BrightLeaf confirmation of receipt, we will delete raw request logs tied to the user within 5 business days, retaining only the ledger and hashed identifiers.

6) Security controls and lineage
   - All exports are logged in our audit trail and stored in an encrypted bucket; access can be restricted to named BrightLeaf contacts.

I'll attach the internal guidance PDF that codifies the above and the runbook for performing the export. Laura — can your team confirm the 5-business-day deletion window is operationally achievable and whether we need an approval ticket for compliance?

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the question and for the attachments. Quick plan we can execute once BrightLeaf confirms: 

1) Redwood will retain invoice PDFs and the billing ledger (invoice lines, amounts, tax) for 7 years to satisfy accounting and audit obligations. Those records are immutable for that retention window.

2) For the deletion request you referenced, we will:
   - Produce an export (CSV + PDFs) containing invoice_id, billing_period, total_tokens charged, and a hashed_customer_id value for reconciliation.
   - Deliver the export securely (please confirm preference: SFTP or secure DocuSign link).
   - After BrightLeaf confirms receipt, Redwood will delete raw request-level logs and any PII tied to the specified user within 5 business days. We will retain only the billing ledger and the hashed identifier (no prompt text, no IPs).

3) If this request is for an ongoing audit or legal hold, please send an authorization from BrightLeaf's legal/finance team and we will freeze deletion until you notify us to resume.

Next steps for you: reply to confirm (a) you want the export and purge flow above, and (b) preferred secure delivery method. Once we have that, we will open the export ticket and share the delivery ETA (typically 2 business days to generate the reconciliation export).
